designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, accurate icon set with confident condensed type; the grid-of-doom versus the deadpan PROBABLY FINE punchline reads in one second from across a room and sells to drivers, mechanics and anyone in denial. On the tee, though, the 20 small labels shrink to unreadable specks, and the check-engine joke is a crowded genre, so it depends on execution more than idea.
designs.fix: Drop the labels (the icons carry it) or cut to 12 bigger lights so the grid holds at chest scale, and enlarge PROBABLY FINE so it anchors the print.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The strongest of the three: a true, warmly observed dog ritual, the repeated 'Turn around.' builds a real comic rhythm, and 'Sigh.' lands the ending. The brush drawings are lively and consistent and the serif italics feel bookish and giftable. My one worry is that the thin lines and small captions get faint at tee size, especially white on black.
designs.fix: Thicken the brush strokes and enlarge the captions by about 30%, and scale the whole print up to fill more of the back so the steps read from a few metres away.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Well drawn: a crisp tabby with good expressions (the side-eye in panel 2, the smug closed eyes in panel 3) and clear instruction-manual staging that needs no words. But cat-prefers-the-box is one of the most familiar cat jokes there is, the fine stripe hatching fills in at print size, and the tall narrow strip sits small and lonely on the shirt.
designs.fix: Add a fresh twist or a dry caption (e.g. a manual-style title or a price tag on the bed), and bolden the linework and stripes so the cat survives at tee scale.
